transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), John Reyes (MountainView PM), Maria Alvarez (Data Scientist), Tom Bowers (Platform Eng)
Links referenced: Redwood eval spreadsheet (https://redwood.sheets/example-eval), prompt set S3 (s3://mvh-poc/prompt_sets/v2), security pack (link shared in chat)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm with Priya our SE. Quick check-in on the weekly quality eval for the POC. How's everyone doing?
00:12 John: Good thanks, yeah — we ran the 500-sample reg set yesterday, got some interesting failures, wanted to walk through them.
00:25 Priya: Great, do you mind if I share my screen? I can pull up the eval spreadsheet and we can step through the examples.
00:34 Maria: Go ahead, I'm on mobile but can follow the sheet.
00:42 Priya: (screen shares) ok opening the sheet, there's a tab called "regression_2026_03_03" — looks like most failures cluster on the reimbursement prompt templates.
00:55 John: Right, the outputs are hallucinating payer codes sometimes, or merging fields incorrectly. Example row 123 shows merging CPT code with diagnosis text.
01:10 Alex: Got it, that's consistent with earlier notes around structured extraction being brittle when prompts vary. Did you use the new guardrail prompts Priya sent last week?
01:22 John: We used v1 of the guardrails, not the updated ones. Maria started with v1 then manually corrected a subset.
01:34 Priya: Okay that's helpful — the v2 guardrails include an explicit extraction schema and an early-stop clause if confidence is low. I pushed examples to the prompt set at s3://mvh-poc/prompt_sets/v2 — Maria, can you confirm you have access?
01:47 Maria: I do, I saw a couple examples but I didn't swap them into the runner yet. I'll switch and re-run after this call.
01:56 Tom: Quick infra note — when you do re-run, please tag the results with the model hash and instance id, we need that to map performance to dedicated vs hosted runs.
02:10 Priya: Good call. For the POC we've been testing both hosted rtx-4000 small instance and a dedicated quantized instance; latency's been ok but cost for high throughput is the concern.
02:25 Alex: Maybe helpful to recap what success looks like for your team so we can prioritize scoring. John?
02:31 John: Sure — primary is extraction accuracy >= 95% F1 on the final prompt set, secondary is median latency < 300ms for single-request transactions, and tertiary is predictable monthly cost under our budget.
02:44 Maria: We're also measuring hallucination rate and schema consistency; we flagged anything that deviates from the schema as critical.
02:55 Priya: Understood. On the current 500-sample run, top-line accuracy was 91%, hallucination rate about 4.5%, median latency ~320ms on hosted.
03:12 Alex: So close on accuracy, latency slightly over — Priya, thoughts on tuning?
03:18 Priya: A couple of levers: more explicit priming and few-shot examples, tighter extraction templates, and we can try a small temperature reduction. Also quantization profile change on dedicated instance improved tail latency in our last internal tests.
03:36 John: If we tighten prompts, do we risk breaking coverage for the edge cases? A lot of our data is messy free-text from clinical notes.
03:47 Priya: Good point — we should keep a diverse dev set. Suggest we create a subset of edge-case prompts and run a separate guardrail pass that does fallback to a conservative "flag for human review" path.
04:05 Alex: Also recommend adding a confidence threshold that triggers the fallback. We can supply a simple scoring rule in the eval sheet.
04:15 Maria: Speaking of scoring, can we discuss the rubric? Some of our raters disagree on partial matches.
04:23 Priya: In the sheet there's a scoring column: exact match = 1.0, partial field match = 0.7, wrong = 0.0. We can add a free-text notes column for edge cases.
04:36 Maria: Could we add a weighted F1 where certain fields (payer, CPT) are higher weight?
04:42 Alex: Absolutely — add a weight column per field in the sheet and we can compute weighted F1. Priya can show formula.
04:52 Priya: I'll add the formula. (typing) ok done, weights implemented for payer and CPT at 1.5x.
05:03 John: Nice. One of our concerns is regression between model versions. The last model bumped increased BLEU-ish metrics but degraded extraction.
05:15 Priya: That's classic — generation metrics don't always correlate with structured-extraction quality. We recommend test harness that does per-prompt scoring and flags regressions beyond a threshold.
05:27 Tom: On the infra side, we need to know if the regressions were due to model change or prompt/temperature changes. Can Redwood provide model artifact hashes and config used for each run?
05:38 Alex: Yes — we'll include model hash, config (temp, top_p), and runtime id in the export. We'll stitch that into the eval sheet so you can filter.
05:46 Maria: Perfect. Another question: privacy and logs — are we comfortable with any PHI being sent to hosted? We need clarity for our compliance folks.
05:59 Alex: Understood — for POC we can enable token redaction and a short retention policy. For production, our Private offering supports VPC and on-prem options and we have KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share the security pack.
06:15 John: Can you confirm SOC2 scope and whether audit logs capture prompt/response pairs? Our auditors will ask.
06:23 Alex: SOC2 Type II is in our security doc; logs include metadata and can include full prompt/response if you opt in — by default we redact certain fields. I'll send the SOC2 summary and a bit on log retention in the next email.
06:36 Priya: Back to quality — Maria, when you re-run with v2 guardrails, could you isolate the top 50 failures and paste a few anon examples in the sheet? That will help our tuning.
06:49 Maria: Yes, I'll do that. Also I'll mark which failures are schema vs hallucination.
06:55 John: There were also a couple of objections from our security team around SSO and RBAC for the console. They want SAML + SCIM provisioning.
07:05 Alex: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync; we can open an entitlement ticket for you. Priya can include the SAML config doc.
07:14 Priya: Will do. Tom — anything on networking?
07:18 Tom: Just the VPC peering checklist, we need CIDR ranges and whether Redwood requires any firewall rules. Also curious about egress IP stability.
07:27 Alex: We'll include the VPC peering checklist and note egress IP options for dedicated/private.
07:32 John: Circling back to scoring — can Redwood run an automated daily regression check and email a weekly summary? That would save our team time.
07:42 Priya: Yes, we can enable daily eval jobs against your canonical prompt set and send a summary report; it's additive to the POC. I'll outline cadence in the follow-up.
07:52 Maria: For the daily run, what model variants will you compare? Hosted latest vs stable deploy?
07:58 Priya: We can do hosted-latest, hosted-stable, and a dedicated quantized variant. We'll add the model ids into the sheet.
08:06 John: Great. A couple specific failures I want to highlight: rows 98-105 on the reimbursement tab show date normalization issues, the model sometimes outputs '03/04' without year. That's a downstream parsing issue.
08:22 Priya: We can add an explicit date-format normalization step in the prompt; also post-process with a lightweight deterministic parser for ambiguous dates.
08:33 Alex: For edge-case mitigation, we often add a verification prompt that asks the model to confirm extracted dates in ISO format; if not, fallback to human review.
08:44 Maria: That makes sense. We'll try that.
08:49 John: On the subject of cost, any early estimates for dedicated instances at our target throughput (1.2k reqs/min)?
08:58 Priya: Preliminary numbers: dedicated quantized pool is about 40% cheaper per token at target throughput versus hosted with autoscaling, but depends on sequence lengths; we'll share a cost model spreadsheet.
09:12 Alex: We'll send a cost breakdown by model variant and quantization profile.
09:18 Tom: One more infra ask: if we run a canary on dedicated, can we run it in our dev VPC with peering? We want to test network latency.
09:28 Priya: Yes, VPC peering for canary is supported for dedicated. We'll coordinate the peering window.
09:35 John: Ok next item — regression alerts threshold. We think a drop of >3% weighted F1 should create an alert. Thoughts?
09:45 Priya: That's reasonable. We'll default to 3% but make it configurable. Alerts can post to Slack or open tickets in Jira.
09:53 Maria: Slack alert works for us. Also include example false positives handling — sometimes a change in scoring weight triggers a blur.
10:03 Alex: We'll add a change log and require annotation for scoring weight changes.
10:09 John: Let's recap concrete next steps before we run out of time.
10:13 Alex: Sure — Alex to send security docs (SOC2 summary, KMS notes) and the cost model by 2026-03-06. Priya to add weighted F1 formula, update guardrail prompt examples and enable daily eval jobs; she'll share the updated prompt S3 link by 2026-03-05. Maria to run regression with v2 guardrails and post top 50 failures by 2026-03-10. Tom to validate VPC peering checklist and confirm CIDR by 2026-03-09.
10:38 John: Sounds good. Also let's schedule the canary week of 2026-03-16 — we'll confirm exact date after infra validation.
10:46 Alex: Great, we'll send a calendar invite for the canary planning. Any other questions?
10:52 Maria: None from me.
10:55 Tom: All set.
10:58 Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and docs. Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., CPT/CFT), speaker labels approximate, timestamps every ~30-90s. Some proper nouns normalized.

End of transcript.
